translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day dingsi, an edict was issued: In antiquity, when a lone wife harbored resentment, a mountain burned on the northern frontier;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the eighth month, an edict declared: In antiquity, when a lone wife harbored resentment, a mountain burned on the northern frontier;

sentences.zh: 孀妻哀慟，臺傾東國。

translations.literal: when a widowed wife grieved in anguish, a tower toppled in the eastern states.
translations.idiomatic: when a widowed wife grieved in anguish, a tower toppled in the eastern states.

sentences.zh: 良以誠之所動，在微必著；

translations.literal: Truly, where sincerity moves, even the minute must appear;
translations.idiomatic: Truly, where sincerity moves, even the minute must appear;

sentences.zh: 感之所震，雖厚必崩。

translations.literal: where feeling shakes, though thick it must collapse.
translations.idiomatic: where feeling shakes, though thick it must collapse.

sentences.zh: 朕臨察九野，志深待旦，弗能使爛然成章，各如其節。

translations.literal: I oversee the nine fields with deep intent awaiting dawn, yet cannot make brilliance spread into patterns, each keeping its measure.
translations.idiomatic: I oversee the nine fields with deep intent awaiting dawn, yet cannot make brilliance spread into patterns, each keeping its measure.

sentences.zh: 遂令炎精損河，陽偏不施，歲云不稔，咎實朕由。

translations.literal: Thus the fiery essence has damaged the river and the yang principle is not fully applied; the year says the harvest fails—the fault is truly mine.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the fiery essence has damaged the river and the yang principle is not fully applied; the year says the harvest fails—the fault is truly mine.

sentences.zh: 太官供膳，宜從貶撤。

translations.literal: The Imperial Butcher’s provisions should follow reduction and withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Butcher’s provisions should follow reduction and withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 近道刑獄，當親料省。

translations.literal: Recent criminal prisons—the emperor should personally examine and reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: Recent criminal prisons—the emperor should personally examine and reduce them.

sentences.zh: 其王畿內及神州所統，可遣尚書與所在共詳；

translations.literal: Within the metropolitan commandery and under the dominion of the sacred province, the Masters of Writing may be sent to examine together with the local authorities;
translations.idiomatic: Within the metropolitan commandery and under the dominion of the sacred province, the Masters of Writing may be sent to examine together with the local authorities;

sentences.zh: 畿外諸州，委之刺史。

translations.literal: the provinces outside the capital are entrusted to the inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: the provinces outside the capital are entrusted to the inspectors.

sentences.zh: 并詳省律令，思存利民。

translations.literal: Let statutes and ordinances also be examined in detail, thinking how to preserve and benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Let statutes and ordinances also be examined in detail, thinking how to preserve and benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 其考讁貿襲，在大明七年以前，一切勿治。

translations.literal: Examinations, dismissals, and inherited penalties before the seventh year of Daming—none shall be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations, dismissals, and inherited penalties before the seventh year of Daming—none shall be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 尤弊之家，開倉賑給。

translations.literal: Among the most afflicted households, open the granaries and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: Among the most afflicted households, open the granaries and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 」乙丑，立第十六皇子子孟為淮南王，第十八皇子子產為臨賀王。

translations.literal: 」On the day yichou, the sixteenth imperial son Zimeng was enfeoffed as Prince of Huainan and the eighteenth Zichan as Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄改。

translations.literal: The text is now emended according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now emended according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 以司州刺史魯爽為豫州刺史 「豫州」各本並作「南豫州」。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Si Lu Shuang was made Inspector of Yu: In all editions this reads 「Southern Yu」.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Si Lu Shuang was made Inspector of Yu: In all editions this reads 「Southern Yu」.

sentences.zh: 廿二史考異云：「案是時無南豫州。

translations.literal: Notes on the Twenty-Two Histories says: 「According to this, there was then no Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Notes on the Twenty-Two Histories says: 「According to this, there was then no Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 『南』蓋衍文也。

translations.literal: The character 「Southern」 is probably a superfluous addition.
translations.idiomatic: The character 「Southern」 is probably a superfluous addition.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉二十二年罷南豫州并壽陽，至孝武大明三年始復分置，中間無南豫者計十年。

translations.literal: Southern Yu was abolished and merged into Shouyang from the twenty-second year of Yongjia; it was not restored until the third year of Daming in Emperor Xiaowu’s reign—a span of about ten years without Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yu was abolished and merged into Shouyang from the twenty-second year of Yongjia; it was not restored until the third year of Daming in Emperor Xiaowu’s reign—a span of about ten years without Southern Yu.

translations.literal: 」Qian’s view is accepted; 「Southern」 is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Qian’s view is accepted; 「Southern」 is now deleted.

sentences.zh: 丁巳 各本並作「丁亥」。

translations.literal: Dingsi: In all editions this reads 「dinghai」.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsi: In all editions this reads 「dinghai」.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「丁亥蓋丁巳誤。

translations.literal: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「dinghai is probably an error for dingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「dinghai is probably an error for dingsi.

sentences.zh: 」按是月壬寅朔，無丁亥，十六日丁巳。

translations.literal: 」According to this, that month’s renyin was the first day; there was no dinghai, while the sixteenth day was dingsi.
translations.idiomatic: 」According to this, that month’s renyin was the first day; there was no dinghai, while the sixteenth day was dingsi.

sentences.zh: 孫說是，今改正。

translations.literal: Sun’s view is accepted; the text is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Sun’s view is accepted; the text is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 戊戌 孫虨宋書考論云：「以前後辛酉己巳推之，戊戌必譌。

translations.literal: Wuxu: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「Judging from the preceding xinyou and following jisi, wuxu must be corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxu: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「Judging from the preceding xinyou and following jisi, wuxu must be corrupt.

sentences.zh: 」按是年七月辛丑朔，二十一日辛酉，二十九日己巳，無戊戌。

translations.literal: 」According to this, that year’s seventh month had xinchou as the first day; the twenty-first was xinyou and the twenty-ninth jisi—there was no wuxu.
translations.idiomatic: 」According to this, that year’s seventh month had xinchou as the first day; the twenty-first was xinyou and the twenty-ninth jisi—there was no wuxu.

sentences.zh: 疑是二十二日壬戌或二十八日戊辰之誤。

translations.literal: It is suspected to be an error for the twenty-second day renxu or the twenty-eighth day wuchen.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected to be an error for the twenty-second day renxu or the twenty-eighth day wuchen.

sentences.zh: 勤盡地利 「勤」各本並作「勸」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: Diligently exhaust the land’s benefit: In all editions 「diligently」 appears as 「urge」; emended according to the Yuan ce 191.
translations.idiomatic: Diligently exhaust the land’s benefit: In all editions 「diligently」 appears as 「urge」; emended according to the Yuan ce 191.

sentences.zh: 三月癸亥 通鑑考異云：「宋本紀、宋略皆作癸亥，下有辛丑。

translations.literal: Third month guihai: Tongjian Collation Notes says: 「The Song annals and Song lüe both read guihai, with xinchou below.
translations.idiomatic: Third month guihai: Tongjian Collation Notes says: 「The Song annals and Song lüe both read guihai, with xinchou below.

sentences.zh: 按長曆，是月戊戌朔，癸亥二十六日，辛丑乃四日也。

translations.literal: According to the long calendar, that month had wuxu as the first day; guihai was the twenty-sixth day, while xinchou was only the fourth day.
translations.idiomatic: According to the long calendar, that month had wuxu as the first day; guihai was the twenty-sixth day, while xinchou was only the fourth day.

sentences.zh: 當作己亥。」

translations.literal: It should read jihai.」
translations.idiomatic: It should read jihai.」

sentences.zh: 二月己丑 下有丙寅。

translations.literal: Second month jichou: Below this appears bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Second month jichou: Below this appears bingyin.

sentences.zh: 按是月壬戌朔，初四日丙寅，二十八日己丑，己丑不當在丙寅前。

translations.literal: According to this, that month had renxu as the first day; the fourth day was bingyin and the twenty-eighth jichou—jichou cannot precede bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, that month had renxu as the first day; the fourth day was bingyin and the twenty-eighth jichou—jichou cannot precede bingyin.

sentences.zh: 疑己丑是乙丑之譌，乙丑為二月初三日。

translations.literal: It is suspected that jichou is a corruption of yichou, and yichou was the third day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected that jichou is a corruption of yichou, and yichou was the third day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 有妨肄業 「肄」各本並作「肆」，據元龜一九五改。

translations.literal: Hinder cultivation: In all editions 「cultivation」 appears as 「indulgence」; emended according to the Yuan ce 195.
translations.idiomatic: Hinder cultivation: In all editions 「cultivation」 appears as 「indulgence」; emended according to the Yuan ce 195.

sentences.zh: 九月丁亥 按本月己丑朔，二十二日庚戌，是月無丁亥。

translations.literal: Ninth month dinghai: According to this month’s jichou as the first day and the twenty-second day gengxu, there was no dinghai in this month.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month dinghai: According to this month’s jichou as the first day and the twenty-second day gengxu, there was no dinghai in this month.

sentences.zh: 以大司馬垣護之為青冀二州刺史 孫虨宋書考論云：「護之不得為大司馬，蓋大司馬僚佐也。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan Huzhi was made Inspector of Qing and Ji: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「Huzhi could not have been Grand Marshal; he was probably a staff officer of the Grand Marshal. The biography of Huzhi is also defective.」
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yuan Huzhi was made Inspector of Qing and Ji: Sun Ao’s Critical Studies on the Book of Song says: 「Huzhi could not have been Grand Marshal; he was probably a staff officer of the Grand Marshal. The biography of Huzhi is also defective.」

sentences.zh: 護之傳並脫。」

translations.literal: The biography of Huzhi is also defective.」
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Huzhi is also defective.」

sentences.zh: 以新除御史中丞王翼為廣州刺史 「王翼」當作「王翼之」。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Supervisor of the Censorate Wang Yi was made Inspector of Guang: 「Wang Yi」 should read 「Wang Yizhi」.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed Supervisor of the Censorate Wang Yi was made Inspector of Guang: 「Wang Yi」 should read 「Wang Yizhi」.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記云：「下大明六年作王翼之，武昌王渾傳作王翼之，此脫『之』字。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai’s collation notes say: 「Below, in the sixth year of Daming, it reads Wang Yizhi; the biography of Prince of Wuchang Hun also reads Wang Yizhi—here the character 「zhi」 has been dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhang Senkai’s collation notes: 「The sixth year of Daming has Wang Yizhi; the biography of Prince of Wuchang Hun also has Wang Yizhi—here the final 「zhi」 has been dropped.

sentences.zh: 」按南北朝人名後之「之」字，有時可省略。

translations.literal: 」According to this, the 「zhi」 in names of the Northern and Southern Dynasties was sometimes omitted.
translations.idiomatic: 」In names of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, this trailing 「zhi」 could sometimes be left out.

sentences.zh: 以北中郎諮議參軍費淹為交州刺史 「北中郎」各本並作「北軍中郎」。

translations.literal: The Consultation Officer of the North Central Commandery Fei Yan was made Inspector of Jiao: In all editions 「North Central Commandery」 appears as 「North Army Central Commandery」.
translations.idiomatic: Consultation Officer of the North Central Commandery Fei Yan, appointed Inspector of Jiao: Every edition reads 「North Army Central Commandery」 instead of 「North Central Commandery」.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記云：「北軍之廢久矣，當是北中郎諮議參軍，衍『軍』字。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai’s collation notes say: 「The North Army has long been abolished; this should be Consultation Officer of the North Central Commandery, with a superfluous 「Army」 character.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai notes: 「The North Army office had long been abolished; the title should be Consultation Officer of the North Central Commandery—the extra 「Army」 is intrusive.

sentences.zh: 」按張說是，今刪「軍」字。

translations.literal: 」Zhang’s view is accepted; 「Army」 is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Following Zhang, 「Army」 is removed from the text.

sentences.zh: 以尚書吏部郎王琨為廣州刺史 各本並脫「郎」字，據南齊書王琨傳補。

translations.literal: The Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Kun was made Inspector of Guang: In all editions the character 「lang」 is missing; it is supplied according to the biography of Wang Kun in the Book of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Kun, made Inspector of Guang: All editions omit 「lang」; the character is restored from the Wang Kun biography in the Book of Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 以丹陽尹劉遵考為尚書右僕射 「右僕射」各本並作「左僕射」，據通鑑改正。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Danyang Liu Zunkao was made Minister of the Right: In all editions this reads 「Minister of the Left」; corrected according to the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Danyang Liu Zunkao, made Minister of the Right: All editions say 「Minister of the Left」; the Comprehensive Mirror supports the correction to Right.

sentences.zh: 按下大明三年春正月己丑，以右僕射劉遵考為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: According to this, on jichou in the first month of spring in the third year of Daming, the Minister of the Right Liu Zunkao was made Colonel of the Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis, on jichou in the first month of Daming year 3, Right Minister Liu Zunkao was made Colonel of the Garrison.

sentences.zh: 劉遵考傳，孝建三年，為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the biography of Liu Zunkao, in the third year of Xiaojian he was Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao’s biography places him as Minister of the Right in Xiaojian year 3.

sentences.zh: 則作「右僕射」為是。

translations.literal: Thus 「Minister of the Right」 is correct.
translations.idiomatic: 「Minister of the Right」 is therefore the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 以東揚州為揚州 「為」各本並作「隸」。

translations.literal: Eastern Yang was made Yangzhou: In all editions 「made」 appears as 「subordinated to」.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yang made Yangzhou: All editions read 「subordinated to」 for 「made」.

sentences.zh: 按州郡志，「孝建元年，分揚州之會稽、東陽、新安、永嘉、臨海五郡為東揚州。

translations.literal: According to the Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies, 「In the first year of Xiaojian, the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin’an, Yongjia, and Linhai were detached from Yangzhou to form Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies records: 「In Xiaojian year 1, Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin’an, Yongjia, and Linhai were split from Yangzhou to form Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，罷州

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, the province was abolished
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 3 the province was abolished

sentences.zh: (揚州)

translations.literal: (Yangzhou)
translations.idiomatic: (Yangzhou)

sentences.zh: ，以其地為王畿。

translations.literal: , and its territory became the metropolitan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: , and its territory was incorporated into the metropolitan commandery.

sentences.zh: 而東揚州直云揚州」。

translations.literal: While Eastern Yang was simply called Yangzhou」.
translations.idiomatic: While Eastern Yang was referred to simply as Yangzhou」.

sentences.zh: 豫章王子尚傳亦云，大明二年，「以浙江東為揚州」。

translations.literal: The biography of Prince of Yuzhang Zishang also says that in the second year of Daming, 「the lands east of the Zhe River were made Yangzhou」.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Zishang’s biography likewise states that in Daming year 2 「the region east of the Zhe was made Yangzhou」.

sentences.zh: 「隸」字顯誤。

translations.literal: The character 「subordinated to」 is clearly an error.
translations.idiomatic: 「Subordinated to」 is plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 今據通鑑、元龜一九六改。

translations.literal: The text is now emended according to the Comprehensive Mirror and Yuan ce 196.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected per the Comprehensive Mirror and Yuan ce 196.

sentences.zh: 辛丑 各本作「辛巳」，據局本及南史改。

translations.literal: Xinchou: In all editions this reads 「xinsi」; emended according to the bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchou: All editions read 「xinsi」; corrected per the bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 張熷讀史舉正云：「按上書乙未，下書丁未，不當有辛巳，作辛丑是。」

translations.literal: Zhang Huang’s Corrections in Reading History says: 「According to the text above on yiwei and below on dingwei, there cannot be a xinsi between them; xinchou is correct.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huang, Corrections in Reading History: 「With yiwei above and dingwei below, xinsi cannot stand; xinchou is right.」

sentences.zh: 義成太守薛繼考討斬之 廿二史考異云：「案休茂傳，繼考為休茂盡力攻城，及休茂死，詐稱立義，乘驛還都，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: Administrator of Yicheng Xue Jikao attacked and beheaded him: Notes on the Twenty-Two Histories says: 「According to the biography of Xiumao, Jikao exerted himself to the utmost in attacking the city for Xiumao; when Xiumao died, he falsely claimed to have raised righteousness and rode the post relay back to the capital; the matter was exposed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Yicheng Xue Jikao “attacked and beheaded him”: Qian Daxin’s Notes on the Twenty-Two Histories observes that in Xiumao’s biography Jikao pressed the siege on Xiumao’s side; after Xiumao died he falsely claimed a loyal rising and rushed to the capital by post, was exposed, and executed.

sentences.zh: 則繼考乃黨於休茂者，紀所書誤。

translations.literal: Thus what the annals record is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The annals therefore err.

sentences.zh: 南史云參軍尹玄慶起義斬之，為得其實。

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties says the Consultation Officer Yin Xuanqing raised righteousness and beheaded him, which accords with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties, attributing the deed to Consultation Officer Yin Xuanqing, matches what actually happened.

sentences.zh: 」按休茂傳，言尹玄慶既斬休茂，繼考以兵脅行府州事劉恭之作啟，言繼考起義，因得封賞，尋事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: 」According to the biography of Xiumao, after Yin Xuanqing had beheaded Xiumao, Jikao used troops to coerce the acting prefect of the commandery and province Liu Gongzhi into writing a memorial saying Jikao had raised righteousness; he thereby received enfeoffment and reward, but soon the matter was exposed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: 」In Xiumao’s biography, once Yin Xuanqing killed Xiumao, Jikao coerced the acting prefect Liu Gongzhi into memorializing a false “righteous rising” by Jikao; he was rewarded, then exposed and executed.

sentences.zh: 蓋國史誤仍當日記注，沈約竟不追改，而於休茂傳則詳述其事始末。

translations.literal: Probably the national history mistakenly retained the daily record of the time; Shen Yue never pursued correction, yet in the biography of Xiumao he narrates the affair from beginning to end in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The national history likely preserved a mistaken daily record; Shen Yue did not revise the annals, though Xiumao’s biography tells the whole story.

sentences.zh: 茲焉時矣 各本並作「茲時篤矣」，據元龜一九四改。

translations.literal: The time is now: In all editions this reads 「the time is earnest indeed」; emended according to Yuan ce 194.
translations.idiomatic: “The time is now”: All editions read 「the time is earnest indeed」; Yuan ce 194 supplies the emendation.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射護軍將軍劉延孫卒 「左僕射」各本並作「右僕射」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Minister of the Left and Colonel of the Guard Liu Yansun died: In all editions this reads 「Minister of the Right」; emended according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Left and Colonel of the Guard Liu Yansun died: All editions say 「Minister of the Right」; the History of the Southern Dynasties is followed.

sentences.zh: 按前五年十月以劉延孫為尚書左僕射，見同卷。

translations.literal: According to this, in the tenth month of the fifth year Liu Yansun was made Minister of the Left, as seen in the same scroll.
translations.idiomatic: As noted earlier in this scroll, in the tenth month of year 5 Liu Yansun became Minister of the Left.

sentences.zh: 丁卯詔上林苑內民庶丘墓欲還合葬者 各本並脫「丁卯詔」三字，據南史補。

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict regarding commoners’ tombs in the Shanglin Park who wished to return for joint burial: In all editions the three characters 「dingmao edict」 are missing; supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Dingmao edict on Shanglin Park tombs: All editions omit 「dingmao edict」; restored from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按是月戊申朔，二十日丁卯。

translations.literal: According to this, that month’s wushen was the first day; the twentieth day was dingmao.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on wushen; dingmao fell on the twentieth day.

sentences.zh: 壬戌 各本並作「壬寅」。

translations.literal: Renxu: In all editions this reads 「renyin」.
translations.idiomatic: Renxu: All editions read 「renyin」.

sentences.zh: 據南史、建康實錄、元龜二０七改。

translations.literal: Emended according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Yuan ce 207.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected per the History of the Southern Dynasties, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Yuan ce 207.

sentences.zh: 按是月丙午朔，無壬寅，十七日壬戌。

translations.literal: According to this, that month’s bingwu was the first day; there was no renyin, while the seventeenth day was renxu.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on bingwu; there was no renyin—the seventeenth day was renxu.

sentences.zh: 普加沾賚 「沾」各本並作「洽」，據元龜一九七改。

translations.literal: Broadly add bounty: In all editions 「bounty」 appears as 「harmony」; emended according to Yuan ce 197.
translations.idiomatic: “Broadly add bounty”: All editions read 「harmony」 for 「bounty」; Yuan ce 197 is followed.

sentences.zh: 其罪甚重辟者 「甚」通鑑作「應」，似是。

translations.literal: Those whose crimes merit the heaviest punishments: In the Comprehensive Mirror 「merit」 appears as 「should」—probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes meriting the heaviest punishments: The Comprehensive Mirror’s 「should」 for 「merit」 is probably right.

sentences.zh: 丙申 各本「丙申」上有「秋七月」。

translations.literal: Bingshen: In all editions 「bingshen」 is preceded by 「seventh month of autumn」.
translations.idiomatic: Bingshen: All editions prefix this with 「seventh month of autumn」.

sentences.zh: 按是年七月甲戌朔，初二日乙亥，二十三日丙申。

translations.literal: According to this, that year’s seventh month had jiaxu as the first day; the second day was yihai and the twenty-third day bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: That year’s seventh month began on jiaxu; the second day was yihai, the twenty-third bingshen.

sentences.zh: 上已有「七月乙亥」，此「秋七月」三字衍，今刪。

translations.literal: Above there is already 「seventh month yihai」; these three characters 「seventh month of autumn」 are superfluous and are now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: 「Seventh month yihai」 already appears above; the extra 「seventh month of autumn」 is deleted.

sentences.zh: 可即開行倉 元龜一九五及二０五無「行」字。

translations.literal: The traveling granaries may immediately be opened: Yuan ce 195 and 205 lack the character 「traveling」.
translations.idiomatic: “Open the traveling granaries at once”: Yuan ce 195 and 205 omit 「traveling」.

sentences.zh: 東諸郡大旱 「大旱」各本並作「大獄」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Great drought in the eastern commanderies: In all editions 「great drought」 appears as 「great prisons」; emended according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: “Great drought in the eastern commanderies”: All editions read 「great prisons」; the History of the Southern Dynasties is followed.

sentences.zh: 洪頤煊諸史考異云：「大獄，當從南史作大旱。

translations.literal: Hong Yixuan’s Critical Studies on the Various Histories says: 「Great prisons should follow the History of the Southern Dynasties and read great drought.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yixuan, Critical Studies on the Various Histories: 「Great prisons should be emended to great drought

sentences.zh: 故下文遣使開倉賑恤。」

translations.literal: Hence below envoys are sent to open granaries and provide relief.」
translations.idiomatic: which explains the order below to open granaries and relieve distress.」

sentences.zh: 壬寅 按是月壬申朔，無壬寅，當有誤。

translations.literal: Renyin: According to this, that month’s renshen was the first day; there was no renyin—there must be an error.
translations.idiomatic: Renyin: That month began on renshen, so renyin cannot be correct—an error is likely.

sentences.zh: 遠近販鬻米粟者 各本並脫「粟」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Those who sell rice and grain from far and near: In all editions the character 「grain」 is missing; supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants selling rice and grain near and far: All editions drop 「grain」; the History of the Southern Dynasties restores it.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為撫軍將軍 各本並脫「南」字，據子鸞傳補。

translations.literal: Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin’an Ziluan was made General Who Pacifies the Army: In all editions the character 「Southern」 is missing; supplied according to the biography of Ziluan.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xu Inspector Prince of Xin’an Ziluan, made General Who Pacifies the Army: All editions omit 「Southern」; Ziluan’s biography supplies it.

sentences.zh: 若濟拯不時 「濟」各本並作「溫」，據元龜一九五改。

translations.literal: If relief is not timely: In all editions 「relief」 appears as 「warm」; emended according to Yuan ce 195.
translations.idiomatic: “If relief is not timely”: All editions read 「warm」 for 「relief」; Yuan ce 195 is followed.
